author: Eric Berne
provenance: Structured reference material (paraphrased, no verbatim reproduction).

slices.summary: Definition of an ulterior transaction: two levels running at once (social + psychological). The words are one thing; the actual message is underneath. Berne claims games are always built on ulterior transactions.
slices.usageNote: Load-bearing for the chapter's first half.

slices.summary: Formal technical definition of a game as an ongoing series of complementary ulterior transactions progressing to a predictable payoff. Four structural features: thesis, antithesis, dynamics, payoff. Berne's six payoff types are named in the source but must NOT be unpacked here (reserved for Ch4 and beyond).
slices.usageNote: Core teaching material for the chapter's second half. Keep the four-part anatomy; do not expand the payoff taxonomy.

slices.summary: Ch3 scope boundary: only ulterior transactions, formal game definition, four-part anatomy. Stroke theory, life positions, catalog game names are forbidden to this chapter. 'Stroke' may appear once as a forward-pointer.
Continuity discipline. Ch1 reserved names and Ch2 reserved names must not be reused. Ch3 introduces Lena, Victor, Priscilla, Nils, Farida, Imani, Hana, Teodora, Petra, Wole, Jonas.

Hard-depth tension: the antithesis is expensive. Breaking a game takes away the payoff both players use, and if the player has no better source of it, seeing the game is not the same as being able to leave it.
slices.usageNote: Required for hard-depth content; the chapter must refuse to promise that naming the game fixes it.

forbiddenContent: Verbatim or near-verbatim reproduction of Berne's prose.
Any unpacking of stroke theory beyond a single forward-pointer use of the word 'stroke' (Ch4).
Any specific game name from Berne's catalog (NIGYSOB, Alcoholic, Why Don't You Yes But, I'm Only Trying to Help You, etc.) — structural patterns only.
Any reuse of Ch1 or Ch2 character names.
